description: Landlord requests full payment — deposit plus multiple months of rent — before the tenant has viewed the property or signed any agreement.
advice: Never pay any money before viewing a property in person and receiving a signed tenancy agreement. Legitimate landlords and agencies do not require full payment upfront before a viewing.
examples: Send the first three months rent and deposit to secure the property before we arrange the viewing.
The landlord only accepts cash. Pay in full and the keys will be posted to you.

description: The property is listed but viewings are refused or blocked, often with excuses such as current tenants, renovation, or remote landlord.
advice: Always insist on viewing a property before paying any deposit. If a landlord refuses a viewing for any reason, treat this as a strong scam signal and walk away.
examples: Sorry, the current tenant is still moving out. Just pay the holding deposit and I will arrange keys.
We only do virtual viewings. The photos are very accurate — you will love it.

description: The landlord claims to be abroad — on a mission, working overseas, or travelling — and cannot meet in person, show the property, or hand over keys directly.
advice: An overseas landlord is not automatically a scammer, but it is a common cover story. Verify ownership via the Land Registry, ask for video call identification, and use a solicitor or reputable letting agent for any transaction.
examples: I am currently on a missionary trip in Ghana. My agent will courier the keys once payment is confirmed.
I am a surgeon working in the US right now. I will post the keys once you transfer the deposit.

description: The rental price is significantly and suspiciously below the market rate for the area and property type, often used to attract desperate or budget-constrained students.
advice: Check comparable properties on Rightmove, Zoopla, or SpareRoom. If a listing is more than 20–30% cheaper than similar properties in the same postcode, investigate carefully before proceeding.
examples: 3-bedroom flat in central London, £400/month all bills included — available immediately.
Special student price for a lovely double room in Zone 2, only £350pcm.

description: The landlord or agent creates artificial urgency, claiming multiple other interested parties or that the offer expires within hours, pressuring the tenant into paying without proper due diligence.
advice: Legitimate rentals do not require same-day decisions under pressure. If someone is rushing you to pay before you have viewed or received paperwork, this is a red flag. Take your time.
examples: I have five other people interested. You must pay the deposit today or I will give it to someone else.
This offer is only valid until midnight tonight. Don't miss out — it is the best deal in Manchester.

description: All communication is restricted to WhatsApp or similar messaging apps, with no formal email, no agency letterhead, no phone call, and no written contract provided.
advice: Reputable landlords and letting agents communicate via verifiable channels — email, phone, formal letters. WhatsApp-only communication makes it difficult to verify identity and creates no audit trail for disputes.
examples: I do not use email. Please contact me only on WhatsApp for all correspondence.
All details will be sent via WhatsApp. No formal contract needed — we trust each other.

description: The landlord refuses to provide a written Assured Shorthold Tenancy (AST) agreement or any formal written contract, claiming it is unnecessary or asking for a verbal arrangement.
advice: In England, Scotland, and Wales, a written tenancy agreement is standard and legally protects both parties. Never move in or pay any money without a signed AST. Without one, you have very limited legal protection.
examples: I do not bother with contracts — it is just extra hassle. We can do this on a trust basis.
My previous tenants never needed a written agreement. Just pay the deposit and move in.

description: A fraudulent letting agency presents itself as legitimate but is not registered with Propertymark, ARLA, The Property Ombudsman, or another recognised UK redress scheme.
advice: Always verify any letting agency on the Propertymark or ARLA register before paying fees or signing contracts. Check Companies House for registration. Look for a physical office address and search for independent reviews.
examples: We are a fully licensed and ARLA-certified agency — (but not actually listed on any register).
Our agency handles hundreds of properties. Pay the admin fee and we will process your application.
